back: Population: the whole set of items of interest. Sample: a subset of the population used to draw conclusions about it.
A list or map of every member of the population, from which a sample can be chosen.
A sample in which every member of the population has a known (usually equal) chance of selection, chosen by a chance mechanism such as random numbers.
A method is biased if it systematically over- or under-represents part of the population; name who is missed and why it matters for the variable studied.
Number the population, read random numbers of the right length, ignore out-of-range values and repeats until the sample is complete.
$k = \frac{N}{n}$; choose a random start from 1 to $k$, then every $k$th member.
Number from stratum $= \frac{\text{stratum size}}{\text{population size}} \times n$, rounded so the total is $n$.
Probability: simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster. Non-probability: quota, convenience, judgement (bias cannot be measured).
A census surveys everyone (no sampling error but costly, slow, sometimes impossible); a sample is cheaper and quicker.
